objective: Decide whether a token string is accepted.

items.item_text: For the token string AXX, answer ‘accepted’ or ‘not accepted’ and give one sentence of reasoning.
items.response_format: Answer ‘accepted’ or ‘not accepted’ and give one sentence of reasoning.
items.correct_response: Accepted, because the final token is X; the total number of X tokens does not otherwise matter.
items.targeted_misconception: M1: A string is accepted exactly when it contains one X anywhere.
items.expected_distractor_reasoning: Answering ‘not accepted’ because AXX contains two X tokens would be consistent with M1.
alternative_explanations: The learner may have miscounted the X tokens.
The learner may have reversed the response labels.
The learner may have overlooked the final token.
items.interpretation_limit: A response cannot by itself distinguish M1 from counting, reading, or response-label errors and does not establish a learner diagnosis.
items.follow_up_probe: For AXX, identify the final token and explain whether changing the number of earlier X tokens would affect acceptance under the rule.

items.item_text: For the token string XA, answer ‘accepted’ or ‘not accepted’ and give one sentence of reasoning.
items.response_format: Answer ‘accepted’ or ‘not accepted’ and give one sentence of reasoning.
items.correct_response: Not accepted, because the final token is A, not X.
items.targeted_misconception: M1: A string is accepted exactly when it contains one X anywhere.
items.expected_distractor_reasoning: Answering ‘accepted’ because XA contains exactly one X would be consistent with M1.
alternative_explanations: The learner may have read the string from right to left.
The learner may have attended to the presence of X without applying the final-token condition.
The learner may have reversed the response labels.
items.interpretation_limit: A response cannot by itself distinguish M1 from reading-direction, attention, or response-label errors and does not establish a learner diagnosis.
items.follow_up_probe: For XA, identify the final token and state which part of the governing rule determines acceptance.

interpretation_limits: Responses are evidence to investigate, never a diagnosis.
The two responses may reveal a pattern consistent with M1, but alternative explanations must be checked with reasoning and follow-up probes.
